ACVP encapsulation (75: ek, m → c, K), decapsulation (30, incl. modified ciphertexts → implicit rejection K̄), key checks (60)
OpenSSL ML-KEM (python cryptography) agrees: same seed → same ek; encaps in one, decaps in the other, both directions (768 and 1024, 40 runs each)
D: inputs outside the contract are refused — wrong lengths, an ek coefficient ≥ q, a dk with a broken H(ek), d/z of the wrong size
SSH: each hybrid (mlkem768x25519 / mlkem768nistp256 / mlkem1024nistp384) negotiates with asyncssh + OpenSSL ML-KEM, C_INIT / S_REPLY have the draft's exact sizes, a 1 MiB echo round-trips
SSH: repeated key exchanges under mlkem768x25519 (server rekeys every 256 KiB; K is a string in the KDF every time) keep a 3 MiB transfer intact
D/G: a man in the middle flips one ML-KEM ciphertext bit → implicit rejection gives an unrelated K_PQ → the host signature over H fails (hostkey-signature), never a silent session
D: S_REPLY one byte short / one byte long / classical half missing → refused as kex before any ML-KEM work; X25519 half replaced by a low-order point → refused

G: downgrade adversary strips the mlkem* names from BOTH KEXINITs → both sides agree on curve25519, but I_C / I_S are inside H, so the signature check fails; stripping one side only → the server's own DISCONNECT reason is shown
